The cause is upstream, in the retirement ledger, and it is the harness working as designed rather than a defect. The 2022 bridge-year evolution retires 4,097 MW of nuclear on reason='announced' — Byron 1+2 (plant 6023) and Dresden 2+3 (plant 869), whose 2020-vintage EIA-860 rows carry Exelon's 2020-08-27 PJM deactivation dates. Illinois CEJA (P.A. 102-0662) reversed both on 2021-09-15, so PJM actually retired 0 GW of nuclear in the window; but the RC-1B information gate in data.confirmed_retirements.load_announced_reversal_plants keys the reversal on superseding_instrument_date (2021-09-15) against this run's 2020-12-31 vintage cutoff, and therefore correctly declines to suppress the announced exit — its own docstring names this exact case. A forecaster standing at end-2020 would have retired both plants. That 4,097 MW of removed firm nuclear is ~3.8x the I7 shortfall and is also 62 % of the run's 6.645 GW false-retire total, so the I7 FAIL, the false-retire FAIL and the +13 % thermal-retire band miss share this one cause. Declared, NOT absolution, and no band or threshold was touched (rules 1/11/14).
